The recurring friction

What changed
since the last entry?

A revised specification, supplier, production process, or value explanation can change what needs review. Tie the new question to the evidence instead of inheriting yesterday’s answer.

The first test

Compare ten historical SKUs.
Measure the same work.

Review dossiers against prior entries without treating historical filing as proof of correctness. Count material disagreements, evidence gaps, and importer and broker rework separately.

The coverage gate

One lane before
more countries.

Local regulatory content, data permissions, and broker distribution constrain expansion. Multi-country support remains unproven and is outside this starting scope.

Before the next step

A few useful questions.

A clear boundary is part of a useful review.

All questions
Who is this for?

US importer-of-record compliance leads handling recurring goods, multiple suppliers, and a customs broker. The starting test is one permissioned repeat-SKU US import lane.

Does it replace our customs broker?

The proposed dossier is prepared for broker review. The importer retains reasonable-care responsibility, and broker or counsel judgment remains part of the workflow.

What if origin evidence is missing?

The record stays held, with a named owner and next action. Available evidence, reviewed evidence, and preference eligibility are separate states.

A bounded next step

Start with one lane.
Learn from ten SKUs.

Review a permissioned sample with your importer and broker. Choose one offer as the first commercial test.
